thesis: A calm clinical briefing should reveal the next meaningful decision before it reveals the rest of the record. The expediente concentrates active risk, medication and two trend signals in one high-contrast briefing field; the portal translates the same calm identity into today's next meal, one habit signal and the upcoming visit without dashboard overload.

composition: Expediente uses an asymmetric briefing canvas plus a narrow next-step column instead of a uniform card grid.
Portal reduces the surface to a meal sequence, one circular habits signal, one care-team message and the next appointment.
The shared synthetic portrait is cropped to the first portrait and kept at 58px so identity remains discreet and subordinate.
hierarchy: Clinical priority and safety facts appear before visit logistics or contact history.
Large Figtree-like display type marks the primary decision while Plus Jakarta Sans-like body text keeps supporting copy compact.
HbA1c and weight trend are the only prominent clinical metrics; portal progress is limited to 2 of 4 habits.
interaction: A keyboard-operable Expediente/Portal tablist switches populated views and supports Left/Right arrows.
Abrir contexto launches a fixed overlay above either current view without recomposing the background.

Escape and both close targets dismiss the panel; focus returns to the exact trigger with preventScroll, Tab is trapped inside, and reduced-motion preferences collapse animation and transition durations.

expressive_opportunity: Treat the expediente as a composed pre-consultation briefing rather than a stack of interchangeable modules, using one deep ink field to make clinical triage feel focused and deliberate while the portal stays notably quieter.
concrete_risk: The large dark briefing field gives the primary clinical context strong authority, but on smaller laptops it may visually outweigh the next-visit actions and should be tested with real product chrome before selection.

limitations: This is one exploratory direction and does not imply user selection or approval.
No product repository, product session, external service, secret or real patient data was used or changed.
The local file URL was blocked by the browser policy, so verification is static and syntax-focused rather than a browser-rendered walkthrough.
No independent visual-reviewer pass or responsive screenshot comparison was performed in this bounded pilot.
